exactFullStudyName: Recombinant Factor VIIa (rFVIIa) for Acute Hemorrhagic Stroke Administered at Earliest Time (FASTEST) Trial - Part 2
sourceHypothesisText: Phase 3, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of rFVIIa (80 µg/kg, max 10 mg) plus best standard therapy for spontaneous ICH treated within 120 minutes of onset with a positive CTA spot sign, or within 90 minutes regardless of spot sign. Uses emergency research consent (EFIC in the US).
sourceGaps: CT.gov excludes oral anticoagulant (VKA or DOAC) use within 7 days, LMWH within 24 hours, pro-coagulant drugs within 24 hours, symptomatic thrombotic/vaso-occlusive disease within 90 days, recent carotid/coronary/cerebrovascular stenting, and planned comfort care; not all are encoded here.

Registry status rechecked 2026-10-21: RECRUITING; last update posted 2026-08-20 (recorded 2026-10-21). This is the overall study status; local site activation, EFIC community consultation and recruitment availability have not been verified.

FASTEST Part 1 (NCT03496883; ACTIVE_NOT_RECRUITING on 2026-10-21) was reported in Lancet 2026 (PMID 41653933; doi:10.1016/S0140-6736(26)00097-8): stopped for futility, with no 180-day mRS difference (adjusted common OR 1.09, 95% CI 0.79–1.51); life-threatening thromboembolic complications within 4 days in 15 (<5%) vs 4 (1%) participants (RR 3.41, 95% CI 1.14–10.15); ICH growth 3.7 mL lower at 24 h. Part 2 is a separate registry record (which describes it as an extension of the FASTEST Trial) restricted to spot-sign-positive ≤ 120 min or any ≤ 90 min. Emerging evidence, not a guideline recommendation.
